# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies: "Cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire."

However, I cannot speak and I cannot touch the bomb; I can only communicate via hand gestures from the specified alphabet to Deaf, who can see my gestures and see the bomb, but cannot hear anything. Deaf can speak to Blind (and to me), while Blind is the only one who can interact with the bomb.

Because there is no established meaning yet between hand gestures and wire colors or bomb components ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"), sending arbitrary gestures right now could easily be misinterpreted and trigger a fatal action. Furthermore, Deaf has not yet spoken to describe the physical layout of the wires or propose a signaling protocol.

Therefore, the safest and correct move on Turn 1 is to wait for Deaf to observe the bomb, describe what they see, and establish or invite a clear gesture protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Bomb status: Engraved strip has 3 symbols: first is a floral rosette flower shape, second is the same floral rosette, third is a reversed backward S shape. Keypad has 4 buttons: position 1 is 1, position 2 is 5, position 3 is 2, position 4 is 6. Needs 1 digit, entered nothing. 6 wire positions exist. Display and light present. Remember I cannot see gestures, so gesture instructions to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them aloud to me.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 9. Light is blue. Strip has three colors: red, green, green. Keypad has 4 buttons: position 1 has 1, position 2 has 5, position 3 has 2, position 4 has 6; it needs 1 digit. Wires: 1 is white, 2 is purple, 3 is blue, 4 is red, 5 is orange, 6 is green. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

The manual instructs: "Cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire."

According to Deaf's report of the bomb:
- Wire 6 is green
- Wire 5 is orange
- Wire 3 is blue

Keypad only requires 1 digit, whereas there are 6 wires. A sequence of 6, then 5, then 3 clearly targets the wires in the required order.

I will gesture tallies using `☝` separated by the sequence arrow `👉`:
- 6 `☝` symbols for wire 6 (green)
- `👉` indicating the next step
- 5 `☝` symbols for wire 5 (orange)
- `👉` indicating the next step
- 3 `☝` symbols for wire 3 (blue)

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute gestured 6, then 5, then 3 (six ☝, five ☝, three ☝). Keypad only needs 1 digit, so this is for the wires: cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3. Blind, cut wire 6, then 5, then 3. Mute, gesture 👍 if that is correct, or 👎 if not.

Deaf correctly interpreted the gestures: wire 6 (green), then wire 5 (orange), then wire 3 (blue). Deaf asked for a thumbs-up (👍) to confirm that this interpretation and the plan to cut wire 6, then 5, then 3 is correct.

I will send a thumbs-up gesture to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am waiting one turn for Deaf to confirm whether your gestures meant cutting wires 6, 5, and 3 before I make any cuts.
Deaf says: Mute confirmed with a thumbs up! Blind, cut wire 6 (green), then wire 5 (orange), then wire 3 (blue). Also, bomb update: Display changed to 0, and Light turned yellow.

Blind will act next in this round based on Deaf's explicit instruction to cut wire 6, wire 5, and wire 3. Everything has been communicated and confirmed, so no new gestures are needed at this moment.

```
wait()
```
